diagnosis.summary: payment-service p95 latency has spiked from 110 ms to 2900 ms, and order-service is reflecting the same degradation with its own p95 latency rising from 130 ms to 2950 ms. order-service is now returning 5xx errors at a 16.7% rate, with 57 failed dependency calls to payment-service per minute.
diagnosis.root_cause: A severe slowdown in payment-service is the most likely root cause, with order-service errors appearing about 40 seconds after payment-service latency rose (observed sequence from correlated timestamps at 14:32:00 and 14:32:40).
evidence: payment-service p95 latency rose from 110 ms to 2900 ms, a 26.4x increase.
order-service p95 latency to its payment dependency rose from 112 ms to 2950 ms, a 26.3x increase, matching the payment-service degradation.
order-service dependency error count rose from 0 to 57 per minute against a baseline of zero.
order-service 5xx error rate rose from 0.0 to 16.7%, up from a baseline of zero errors.
order-service p95 end-to-end latency rose from 130 ms to 2950 ms, a 22.7x increase above its baseline.
recommended_actions: Inspect payment-service Lambda logs and CloudWatch metrics starting at 14:32:00 to identify the source of the latency spike.
Check payment-service Lambda duration metrics and any downstream integrations it calls for signs of slow execution or external timeouts.
Consider adding or lowering a timeout on order-service calls to payment-service to limit blast radius while the root issue is investigated.
If payment-service cannot recover quickly, evaluate whether order-service can queue or defer payment calls to stop 5xx errors from reaching end users.
Review payment-service cold start counts and throttle counts for anomalies that may explain the latency increase.
